mainTopic: Doubtful נזירות: רבי זירא's attribution to רבי אליעזר, its challenges from בכורות and doubtful liquids, and the new split between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון
overview: The גמרא is working on a contradiction between our משנה, which is strict about unclear vows, and another משנה that treats a doubtful נזירות leniently. רבי זירא explains that the lenient משנה follows רבי אליעזר: a person does not put himself into a doubtful state of holiness. אביי challenges this from the next clause of that משנה, about doubtful בכורות, which a ברייתא forbids to shear or work. רבי זירא answers that a בכור becomes holy by itself, while נזירות depends on a person's choice. The גמרא then raises a stronger problem from the same משנה. A doubtful liquid is called טמא itself, yet a ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר saying liquids have no טומאה at all. This works according to שמואל's reading of that ברייתא but not according to רב's. So the גמרא gives a new answer: the lenient משנה follows רבי יהודה and our strict משנה follows רבי שמעון, as shown by their dispute about a heap of grain that went missing. Finally, the גמרא starts to challenge רבי יהודה from his own ruling about unspecified תרומה, and that challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A person does not put himself into doubt
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא finishes his explanation: according to רבי אליעזר, all the more so a person does not enter himself into a doubtful situation, so a doubtful נזירות is treated leniently.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the more so, a person does not enter himself into a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of רבי זירא's explanation from just before. He is closing his reasoning for why a doubtful נזירות is lenient according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that people do not take on holiness in an unclear way. So if it is doubtful whether someone became a נזיר, we assume he did not mean to accept נזירות in that doubtful case. This is a claim about what a person intends.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so
Brings in, enters
A doubt, an uncertain situation

phrases.english: All the more so
that he does not enter [himself] into a doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי זירא's explanation, which began before this section, of why ספק נזירות is lenient.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the משנה to a specific תנא, רבי אליעזר
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה of ספק נזירות להקל follows רבי אליעזר: a person does not enter himself into a doubt.

steps.title: אביי quotes the next clause about doubtful firstborns
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבי זירא by quoting the end of the same משנה: in a doubtful בכור case, human or animal, the one who wants to take it must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: How did you explain the rule that a doubtful נזירות is lenient? As following רבי אליעזר. Then look at the end of that משנה: with doubtful firstborns, whether human or animal, kosher or non-kosher, whoever wants to take from his fellow must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins an attack on רבי זירא's explanation. Here he only sets up the challenge by quoting the end of the משנה; the actual punch comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the quoted clause only says money is not taken in a doubtful בכור case. The owner keeps the animal or the redemption money, which sounds lenient. אביי is getting ready to show that on the prohibition side, the doubt is not treated leniently.

keyTerms.meaning: You established, you explained the source as following a certain view
Say the end clause of the source
Doubtful firstborns
Whoever wants to take from his fellow must bring proof

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: How did you establish
that a doubtful naziriteship is lenient? As Rabbi Eliezer.
Say the end clause:
Doubtful firstborns,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד בְּכוֹרֵי אָדָם וְאֶחָד בְּכוֹרֵי בְהֵמָה,
phrases.english: whether human firstborns or animal firstborns,
whether non-kosher or kosher,
phrases.notes: A non-kosher firstborn here means a firstborn donkey, the only non-kosher animal with firstborn laws.

phrases.english: whoever takes from his fellow, the proof is upon him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's explanation by bringing in the next clause of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's claim that this משנה treats doubts about holiness leniently, following רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the same משנה deals with doubtful בכורות, we need to check whether it treats that doubt leniently too. The next step will show that it does not.

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids shearing and working doubtful firstborns
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא on that משנה teaches that doubtful firstborn animals may not be sheared or worked, the same as certain firstborns.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught about it: they are forbidden in shearing and work!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי completes his challenge with a ברייתא. Even though the owner keeps the doubtful firstborn, he may not shear it or work with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shearing and working are forbidden only for a holy animal. So on the prohibition side, the doubtful בכור is treated strictly. That clashes with the idea that this משנה treats all doubtful holiness leniently.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught about it, introducing a ברייתא on that משנה
Shearing the wool
Using the animal for work

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a split in the law of a doubtful בכור: lenient about money, strict about the prohibitions. That split is what makes אביי's question sharp.

phrases.english: And it was taught about it:
and they are forbidden in shearing and work!
phrases.notes: 'They' are the doubtful firstborn animals from the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא that turns the quoted clause into a real challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That the תנא of this משנה does not treat every doubt about holiness leniently
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on the משנה of doubtful בכורות, forbidding shearing and work

steps.title: Holiness that comes by itself versus holiness a person creates
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that a בכור becomes holy by itself, while נזירות comes from a person's choice, so they cannot be compared.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Why are you comparing holiness that comes by itself to holiness that comes through a person?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא defends his explanation. He says אביי's case of a doubtful בכור is a different kind of holiness from נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור is holy simply because it was born first; nobody's intention is involved. נזירות happens only because a person decides to take it on. The rule 'a person does not enter himself into a doubt' is about intention, so it applies only to holiness a person creates, not to a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: You compare
Holiness that comes by itself, like a בכור
Holiness that comes through a person's action or decision, like נזירות

steps.whatToRemember: The leniency of ספק נזירות rests on what a person intends: people do not take on holiness while unsure. That reasoning cannot apply to a בכור, whose holiness comes by itself, so the strict rule for a doubtful בכור is not a contradiction.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא is not saying a doubtful בכור is lenient. He agrees it is strict. He is explaining why its strictness does not disprove the leniency for נזירות.

phrases.english: He said to him: Why are you comparing
holiness that comes by itself
to holiness that comes by the hands of a person?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by showing that his case is not comparable.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי assumed all doubtful holiness works the same way, so the strict rule for a doubtful בכור should disprove the leniency for נזירות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Holiness that depends on a person's intent, like נזירות, is not taken on in doubt. Holiness that comes by itself, like a בכור, can apply even in doubt.

steps.title: A new difficulty: the doubtful liquid ruling in the same משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the בכור question and quotes another line of the same משנה: a doubtful liquid is טמא itself but does not make others טמא. This is רבי מאיר's view, and the משנה adds that רבי אליעזר agreed with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty: A doubtful liquid is impure as far as becoming impure itself, but pure as far as making other things impure. These are the words of רבי מאיר, and the same משנה says רבי אליעזר agreed with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the real problem for רבי זירא is somewhere else, and it quotes another ruling from the same משנה. This step is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא said the doubtful rulings in this משנה follow רבי אליעזר. So the גמרא picks a doubtful ruling that is said directly in רבי אליעזר's name, about liquids, and gets ready to test it against what רבי אליעזר says elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: If there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty. It sets aside the earlier question for a stronger one.
A liquid whose טומאה status is in doubt
To become טמא itself
To make other things טמא

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two halves of the ruling. The doubtful liquid IS טמא for itself, but it does NOT pass טומאה on to other things.

phrases.english: Rather, if there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty:
A doubtful liquid,
as for becoming impure itself, it is impure,
as for making others impure, it is pure,
these are the words of רבי מאיר,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר כִּדְבָרָיו.
phrases.english: and so too רבי אלעזר would say like his words.
phrases.notes: The spelling here is אלעזר, but the very next line treats this as the opinion of רבי אליעזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the בכור challenge, which רבי זירא answered in Step 4, and brings a stronger challenge from the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's claim that the doubtful rulings in this משנה follow רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step quotes the ruling that will be tested. The actual attack comes in the next step.

steps.title: Does רבי אליעזר really hold a doubtful liquid is impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי אליעזר truly holds that a doubtful liquid becomes טמא itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does רבי אליעזר really hold that, as for becoming impure itself, a doubtful liquid is impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether the משנה's ruling could really be רבי אליעזר's opinion. The proof for this doubt comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי אליעזר does not hold this, then this doubtful ruling is not his. That would weaken רבי זירא's claim that the whole משנה follows רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: But does he really hold this? It introduces a challenge.

phrases.english: But does רבי אליעזר hold
that as for becoming impure itself, it is impure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the משנה quoted in Step 5 into a direct question about רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that רבי אליעזר agrees a doubtful liquid is טמא itself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי אליעזר holds elsewhere that liquids cannot become טמא at all, a doubtful liquid could never be טמא according to him.

steps.title: A ברייתא: רבי אליעזר holds liquids have no טומאה at all
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר saying that liquids cannot become טמא at all. He supports this with יוסי בן יועזר's testimony that the liquids of the Temple slaughterhouse are pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says, liquids have no טומאה at all. Know that this is so, because יוסי בן יועזר of צרידה testified that the grasshopper called איל קמצא is kosher, and that the liquids of the slaughterhouse are pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source that backs up its question. רבי אליעזר seems to say liquids never become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If liquids have no טומאה at all, it makes no sense for רבי אליעזר to say a doubtful liquid is טמא itself. The testimony that the slaughterhouse liquids are 'pure' is his proof.

keyTerms.meaning: At all
Know that this is so. It introduces a proof.
He testified
Pure or kosher (Aramaic)

phrases.english: But it was taught: רבי אליעזר says:
liquids have no impurity at all.
Know that it is so: for he testified,
יוסי בן יועזר, the man of צרידה,
about the איל קמצא, that it is kosher,
phrases.notes: איל קמצא is a kind of grasshopper.

phrases.english: and about the liquids of the slaughterhouse, that they are pure?
phrases.notes: This means the slaughterhouse in the בית המקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ברייתא that backs up the question in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר does not hold a doubtful liquid is טמא itself
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with רבי אליעזר's statement, supported by יוסי בן יועזר's testimony about the slaughterhouse liquids

steps.title: According to שמואל, the ruling fits well
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this works well according to שמואל. He explains that 'pure' only means the liquids cannot make other things טמא, while they themselves can still become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works out well according to שמואל, who said: 'pure' means they cannot make others impure, but they themselves can become impure. So it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that according to שמואל there is no contradiction. It says 'this works for שמואל', which hints that the other view may still be a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל reads 'pure' in the testimony narrowly: these liquids cannot pass טומאה to others. They can still become טמא themselves. So רבי אליעזר can agree that a doubtful liquid is טמא itself, and רבי זירא's claim holds.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (according to one view). It often hints that another view still has a problem.
Their own טומאה, meaning becoming טמא themselves
Fine, it works well

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how one word, 'pure' (דכן), can mean two different things: fully pure, or only unable to make others טמא. The answer depends on which reading we use.

phrases.english: This works out well according to שמואל, who said:
'pure' means pure from making others impure,
but they do have impurity of their own,
it is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from Steps 6-7, but only according to שמואל's reading of the testimony.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the source: 'pure' means only that the liquids cannot make others טמא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Pure' in the testimony means liquids cannot become טמא at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to שמואל, liquids can become טמא themselves. So the משנה's ruling fits רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: What about רב, who says the liquids are truly pure?
steps.stepSummary: The answer based on שמואל does not work for רב, who holds that the liquids cannot become טמא at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב, who said the liquids are really pure, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the last answer only works for שמואל. According to רב, the problem comes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads יוסי בן יועזר's testimony literally: the liquids of the Temple slaughterhouse cannot become טמא at all. So רבי אליעזר could not say that a doubtful liquid is טמא itself, and the משנה's claim that he agreed makes no sense. This means the whole approach of tying the משנה to רבי אליעזר falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually pure: they cannot become טמא at all
What is there to say? This is a formula for a question with no answer yet

phrases.english: But according to Rav, who said
they are actually pure,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַב דְּאָמַר דְּכַן מַמָּשׁ, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer from step 8 only works for שמואל, not for רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The attempt to explain the משנה according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רב, רבי אליעזר holds that liquids never become טמא. So he could not agree that a doubtful liquid is טמא itself.

steps.title: New answer: a dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the earlier approach. The two משניות simply follow different תנאים: the lenient one follows רבי יהודה, the strict one follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: that משנה follows רבי יהודה, and this משנה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a brand-new answer to the original contradiction. The two משניות just reflect two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, רבי זירא tied the lenient משנה to רבי אליעזר, but steps 6-9 showed that does not fit, at least according to רב. Now the גמרא ties the two משניות to a different pair of תנאים. The משנה that is lenient on a doubtful נזירות follows רבי יהודה, and our משנה, which is strict, follows רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: This one ... and that one. It splits two sources between two opinions

phrases.english: Rather: that one is Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: "That one" is the lenient משנה about a doubtful נזירות.

phrases.english: and this one is Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: "This one" is our משנה, which is strict with unclear vows.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְהָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי זירא's attribution of the lenient משנה to רבי אליעזר, which failed in steps 5-9, with an attribution to רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources between two תנאים (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lenient משנה about doubtful נזירות follows רבי אליעזר, as רבי זירא said.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משניות follow different תנאים who disagree about a doubtful נזירות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This replaces the attribution to רבי אליעזר, which failed in steps 6-9, with a different pair of תנאים. Their disagreement is shown directly in the ברייתא in the next step.

steps.title: Proof: the heap of grain that went missing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון disagree about a doubtful נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: someone said, 'I am a נזיר if this heap has one hundred כור.' He went to measure it and found it was stolen or lost. רבי יהודה permits him, and רבי שמעון forbids him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that these two תנאים really argue about a doubtful נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the heap is gone, nobody can ever know whether the condition came true, so the נזירות is a real doubt. רבי יהודה lets the person act normally, so he is lenient. רבי שמעון forbids him, so he is strict.

keyTerms.meaning: I am hereby a נזיר
A heap of grain
A large measure of volume
Permits / forbids

phrases.english: As it is taught: "I am hereby a nazirite

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בִּכְרִי הַזֶּה מֵאָה כּוֹר״,
phrases.english: if there are in this heap one hundred kor,"
and he went and found it
that it was stolen or that it was lost —
Rabbi Yehuda permits,
and Rabbi Shimon prohibits.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר אִם יֵשׁ בִּכְרִי הַזֶּה מֵאָה כּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 10 that רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון disagree.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה is lenient and רבי שמעון is strict about a doubtful נזירות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a vow tied to the size of a heap that was stolen or lost.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: a doubtful נזירות does not take hold (lenient). רבי שמעון: it does take hold (strict).

steps.title: רבי יהודה against רבי יהודה: unspecified תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה's view that a person does not bring himself into doubt, using his ruling about סתם תרומה in יהודה and the גליל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא sets one ruling of רבי יהודה against another. Did רבי יהודה really say a person does not bring himself into doubt? But רבי יהודה said: unspecified תרומה in יהודה is forbidden, and in the גליל it is permitted, because the people of the גליל do not know the תרומת הלשכה. The reason is that they do not know it,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction inside רבי יהודה's own opinions. It starts to draw an inference from his reason, and the inference continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the heap case, רבי יהודה's reason is that a person does not put himself into a doubtful vow. But when someone vows using unspecified תרומה, he says it is forbidden in יהודה even though the word is unclear. In the גליל it is permitted only because people there do not know about תרומת הלשכה. That suggests that where people do know it, an unclear vow does take hold.

keyTerms.meaning: He raises a contradiction between one source and another
A person does not bring himself into a doubt
Unspecified תרומה, said in a vow without saying which kind
The half-shekel funds collected in the Temple chamber
The reason, often used to start an inference

phrases.english: And he raises a contradiction between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yehuda:
Did Rabbi Yehuda really say
a person does not bring himself into a doubt?
But contrast it with this: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Unspecified teruma in Judea is forbidden,
phrases.notes: This is from our משנה: someone vows that something is to him "like תרומה" without saying which kind.

phrases.english: and in the Galilee it is permitted,
because the people of the Galilee are not familiar
with the teruma of the chamber.
The reason is that they are not familiar;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the consistency of רבי יהודה's position from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's principle that a person does not bring himself into doubt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the תרומה case, he forbids an unclear vow in יהודה and permits it in the גליל only because people there do not know תרומת הלשכה. This implies that an unclear vow does take hold when people know the meaning.
steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not finished here. "טַעְמָא דְּאֵין מַכִּירִין" only begins the inference, and the conclusion comes in the next lines.
